findings.title: setUTCMonth overflows on month-end dates, skipping a month (regression)
findings.explanation: The PR assumes setUTCMonth handles rollover, but it does not clamp the day of month. For a period starting Jan 31, setUTCMonth(1) produces Feb 31, which rolls over to Mar 3 (or Mar 2 in a leap year). Likewise Mar 31 -> Apr 31 -> May 1, Aug 31 -> Oct 1, and so on. The removed code explicitly clamped to the last day of the next month (Jan 31 -> Feb 28/29). With this change, customers anchored on the 29th, 30th or 31st would be billed late or on the wrong day, and the period end would drift. This is a billing correctness regression. Restore the clamping, for example: compute the last day of next month with Date.UTC(year, month + 2, 0) and use Math.min(anchorDay, lastDay) when building the end date. Alternatively, set the date to 1 first, set the month, then set the date to min(anchorDay, daysInMonth).

findings.title: No tests cover month-end edge cases
findings.explanation: The behavior that was removed (clamping for Jan 29/30/31, leap years, and Dec -> Jan year rollover) is exactly what needs regression tests, and the PR adds none. Add tests for Jan 31 (leap and non-leap year), Mar 31, Aug 31, Dec 31 -> Jan 31, and a normal mid-month date, so this kind of change cannot silently break billing.

findings.title: Inconsistent date copying and loss of anchor day across chained periods
findings.explanation: Even with clamping, chaining nextPeriod(end) will permanently shift an anchor of 31 to 28 after February (Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 28). If the original billing anchor day matters, consider passing the anchor day explicitly or storing it separately. This is pre-existing behavior, but worth noting while touching this function. Also, new Date(periodStart) is used for both start and end, which is fine, but could be simplified once the clamping logic is restored.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Simplify next billing period calculation

Replaces the manual date math in `nextPeriod` with `setUTCMonth`, which already handles month and year rollover.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/billing.ts b/src/services/billing.ts
index 81ad02d..eb1824d 100644
--- a/src/services/billing.ts
+++ b/src/services/billing.ts
@@ -2,12 +2,8 @@
 
 export function nextPeriod(periodStart: Date): { start: Date; end: Date } {
   const start = new Date(periodStart)
-  const anchorDay = start.getUTCDate()
-  const year = start.getUTCFullYear()
-  const month = start.getUTCMonth() + 1
-  // Clamp to the last day of the next month, so a period starting on Jan 31 renews on Feb 28/29.
-  const lastDayOfNextMonth = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate()
-  const end = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, Math.min(anchorDay, lastDayOfNextMonth)))
+  const end = new Date(periodStart)
+  end.setUTCMonth(end.getUTCMonth() + 1)
   return { start, end }
 }
```
